source_text: Ἰγνάτιος, ὁ καὶ Θεοφόρος, ἐκκλησίᾳ θεοῦ πατρὸς καὶ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τῇ οὔσῃ ἐν Φιλαδελφίᾳ τῆς Ἀσίας, ἠλεημένῃ καὶ ἡδρασμένῃ ἐν ὁμονοίᾳ θεοῦ καὶ ἀγαλλιωμένῃ ἐν τῷ πάθει τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν ἀδιακρίτως καὶ ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει αὐτοῦ πεπληροφορημένῃ ἐν παντὶ ἐλέει, ἣν ἀσπάζομαι ἐν αἵματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἥτις ἐστὶν χαρὰ αἰώνιος καὶ παράμονος, μάλιστα ἐὰν ἐν ἑνὶ ὦσιν σὺν τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ καὶ τοῖς σὺν αὐτῷ πρεσβυτέροις καὶ διακόνοις ἀποδεδειγμένοις ἐν γνώμῃ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, οὓς κατὰ τὸ ἴδιον θέλημα ἐστήριξεν ἐν βεβαιωσύνῃ τῷ ἁγίῳ αὐτοῦ πνεύματι.
thought_title: Greeting to the Church in Philadelphia
orientation: Ignatius opens his letter to the church in Philadelphia, greeting them as a church established in God's concord and rejoicing in Christ's passion and resurrection.
pass_a_gloss: Ignatius, the [one] also [called] God-bearer, to the church of God [the] Father and of [the] Lord Jesus Christ, the [one] being in Philadelphia of Asia, [the one] having been shown mercy and having been established in [the] concord of God and rejoicing in the passion of our Lord without doubting and in his resurrection having been fully assured in every mercy, which [church] I greet in [the] blood of Jesus Christ, which is joy eternal and abiding, especially if they are in one [mind] with the bishop and with the council of elders with him and deacons having been appointed in [the] purpose of Jesus Christ, whom according to his own will he established in firmness by his holy Spirit.

choices.why: The name is a title meaning 'bearing God'; rendering it as a title preserves the wordplay Ignatius uses of himself.
The perfect passive participle indicates a completed state of having received mercy; the passive voice is preserved.
The adverb modifies the rejoicing, indicating the manner in which the church rejoices in the passion; 'without doubting' captures the sense of no wavering or division.
The perfect passive participle conveys a settled state of full conviction; 'fully assured' captures the sense of complete confidence.
The phrase 'in one' refers to unity of mind or purpose; adding 'mind' clarifies the sense without altering the claim.
The perfect passive participle indicates an official appointment already made; 'appointed' preserves the formal sense.

pass_b_english: Ignatius, who is also called Theophorus, to the church of God the Father and of the Lord Jesus Christ at Philadelphia in Asia. This church has received mercy and is established in the concord of God. It rejoices without doubting in the passion of our Lord, and through his resurrection it has been fully assured of every mercy. I greet this church in the blood of Jesus Christ, which is eternal and abiding joy, especially if they are of one mind with the bishop and with the council of elders and the deacons who have been appointed alongside him according to the purpose of Jesus Christ. He established these leaders in firmness by his Holy Spirit according to his own will.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'council of elders' for πρεσβυτέριον; here plural πρεσβυτέροις should still use the fixed term.
last_rejected.ruling: πρεσβυτέροις is plural of πρεσβύτερος ('elder'), not πρεσβυτέριον ('council of elders'); 'elders' is correct.

last_rejected.quote: He established these leaders in firmness
last_rejected.source_quote: οὓς κατὰ τὸ ἴδιον θέλημα ἐστήριξεν ἐν βεβαιωσύνῃ τῷ ἁγίῳ αὐτοῦ πνεύματι
last_rejected.why: The antecedent of 'οὓς' is the bishop, elders, and deacons together, but 'these leaders' loses the specific connection. More critically, 'ἐν βεβαιωσύνῃ' means 'in steadfastness/firmness' but the English 'in firmness' is vague. The main issue: the Greek says 'whom he established in steadfastness by his Holy Spirit'—the dative 'τῷ ἁγίῳ αὐτοῦ πνεύματι' is instrumental ('by his Holy Spirit'), but the English structure makes it sound like 'in firmness by his Holy Spirit' which is awkward.
last_rejected.fix: whom he established in steadfastness by his Holy Spirit
last_rejected.ruling: No meaning change or loss. 'These leaders' correctly renders οὓς; 'in firmness by his Holy Spirit' accurately reflects ἐν βεβαιωσύνῃ τῷ ἁγίῳ πνεύματι. Awkwardness is stylistic, not semantic.
